Figure 1. Overview of Hybrid Masking Adaptation of LLaDA-V for GUI Grounding. (a) The adapted framework takes a natural-
language instruction and a GUI screenshot (either from web, desktop, or mobile interfaces) as input. LLaDA-V trained with the linear
masking predicts the action type, optional type in text, and anchor coordinates (x_1, y_1). LLaDA-V model trained with the full deter-
ministic masking predicts the remaining bounding-box coordinates (x_2, y_2) conditioned on the image, instruction, and anchor. (b) Linear
Masking Phase: action and anchor tokens in the response are randomly masked according to the linear masking during the forward cor-
ruption process during training for coarse grounding during training. (c) Deterministic Masking Phase: all response tokens are fully
masked in the forward corruption process during training, and LLaDA-V predicts the bounding-box extent during denoising.

2.2.2. Discrete Diffusion Models                                 Our work builds on LLaDA-V [48], a discrete DVLM that
Discrete diffusion models operate directly on token-level        combines visual instruction tuning with masked discrete
categorical distributions. The forward process progressively     diffusion. The architecture comprises a language tower
masks tokens, and the reverse process reconstructs them          LLaDA [31], a vision tower SigLIP-2 [43, 49], and a
through iterative denoising. Prior works differ mainly in        two-layer MLP projector aligning visual embeddings with
their noise schedules and transition mechanisms: D3PM [2]        the language token space. LLaDA-V is trained on mul-
uses uniform categorical transitions, DiffusER [34] models       timodal dialogue data involving image–text interactions.
reversible text edits, and others [31, 36, 52] adopt masking-    For a two-turn example, each instance is represented as
based corruption. However, these methods focus solely on         (v, p^1_0, r^1_0, p^2_0, r^2_0), where v is the image embedding, p^1_0, p^2_0
text as input and do not address multimodal text generation,     are textual prompts for the first and second turns, and r^1_0, r^2_0
which is essential for interactive vision–language tasks.        are their corresponding responses. The model reconstructs
masked tokens using the following discrete diffusion objec-                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       The number of sequential blocks used to generate the output
tive:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             sequence. Tokens within each block are generated in paral-
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  lel, and the block length must be greater than or equal to
    \begin {split} -\mathbb {E}_{\substack { v, t, p^1_0, r^1_0, r^1_t,\\ p^2_0, r^2_0, r^2_t}} \Bigg [ \frac {1}{t} \sum _{i=1}^{L_{r1}} \sum _{j=1}^{L_{r2}} \mathbf {1}\big [r^{1,i}_{t} = [M] \wedge r^{2,j}_{t} = [M]\big ] \\ \times \log p_\theta \big (r^{1,i}_{0}, r^{2,j}_{0} \mid v, p^1_0, r^1_t, p^2_0, r^2_t\big ) \Bigg ] \end {split} \tag {1}    the generation length. When the two are equal, generation
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  is fully parallel; when the block length is larger, the model
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  generates in a semi-autoregressive manner.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      We adopt LLaDA-V as our base model owing to its
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  strong performance in multimodal reasoning and visual in-
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (1)     struction following. Moreover, at the time of our study, it
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  was the only publicly available discrete DVLM, making it
   where r^1_t, r^2_t are masked responses at diffusion step t,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   the most suitable and practical foundation for adaptation to
and [M] denotes the mask token, and i, j are the indexes of                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       GUI grounding.

fusion Steps (Diff. Steps), predefined by the user before            bounding box correctly localizes the target element. A pre-
inference, and Converged Steps (Conv. Steps), the number             diction is considered correct if the center of the predicted
of steps after which denoising stops once the model reaches          bounding box lies within the ground-truth bounding box.
a confident prediction. Our initial study (Table 2) shows            We use the center point rather than the full area to better
that setting all inference parameters to 64 yields the best          represent action precision and robustness, as small bound-
performance, which we adopt for subsequent experiments.              ary misalignments in GUI environments often do not affect
In later results (Figure 3 and Table 4), we report Converged         task success. This criterion provides a reliable and practi-
Steps as they reflect the actual number of steps required by         cal measure of GUI grounding accuracy. For equations look
LLaDA-V to generate a stable output. For more informa-               Appendix D

5.4. Evaluation Metrics
                                                                     6.1. Discrete DVLMs Can Perform GUI Grounding
We evaluate model performance using two metrics: Action-
Type F1 and Step Success Rate (SSR). Action-Type F1                  We first evaluate whether a discrete DVLM model LLaDA-
measures how accurately the model predicts the intended              V can perform single step GUI grounding, when trained
action type among the three possible categories: lclick,             with the default Linear Masking. As shown in Table 2,
hover, and type in. It reflects the balance between pre-             LLaDA-V 8B, fine-tuned on only 7k Mind2Web samples,
cision and recall in classifying actions correctly.                  achieves an SSR of 80.67% and an action-type F1 of 99%
Figure 3. GUI Data Scaling behavior of LLaDA-V 8B trained with Linear Masking: Comparison between LLaDA-V 8B trained
on 7k web GUI samples from Mind2Web and 120k mobile, web and desktop GUI samples across four GUI grounding datasets. M2W:
Mind2Web, SWT: ScreenSpot-Web-Text, SWI: ScreenSpot-Web-Icon, VWA: Visual Web Arena. Left plot shows Step Sucess Rate (SSR),
the center plot shows the number of Converged Steps, and right shows average Inference Latency measured in seconds. Training with
large-scale GUI multi-domain data improves SSR, reduces the number of Converged Steps required to produce a highly confident output
while reducing Inference Latency, demonstrating better generalization and efficiency across GUI domains.

While our work proposes an improved grounding technique
for diffusion vision–language models, it remains an early        11. Appendix D
step toward bridging the gap with AR approaches. Al-
though diffusion models demonstrate promising structured         We evaluate model performance using two metrics: Action-
grounding capabilities, they still lag behind AR models in       Type F1 and Step Success Rate (SSR).
latency and accuracy, possibly due to the latter’s exten-
sive grounding-specific pretraining and optimized decod-         Action-Type F1. The Action-Type F1 measures how

tion prediction, where the output length is short and the la-    among the three possible categories (lclick, hover, and
tency difference remains modest. However, extending to           type in). It is defined in terms of precision and recall as:
multi-step action prediction, which involves longer output
sequences, will likely present different outcomes. Future                \text {Precision} = \frac {TP}{TP + FP}, \quad \text {Recall} = \frac {TP}{TP + FN}, 
work should explore grounding-specific pretraining, effi-
cient diffusion decoding strategies, and architectural refine-                           \text {F1} = \frac {2 \times \text {Precision} \times \text {Recall}} {\text {Precision} + \text {Recall}}, 
ments to scale diffusion-based models toward multi-action
GUI grounding.                                                   where TP , FP , and FN represent true positives, false

Figure 4. Effect of data annotation quality on grounding accuracy. The figure compares predictions from LLaDA-V trained with default
linear masking using the Mind2Web train split with and without cropped images and OCR-based annotations. The top example, trained
without OCR text-based annotations and cropping, produces an inaccurate bounding box due to inconsistent icon-level targets and high-
resolution inputs. The bottom example, trained with cropped images and OCR-guided text annotations, provides more stable supervision,
allowing the model to correctly localize the target element. The green bounding box is the ground truth and the red one is the prediction.

Figure 5. Effect of hybrid masking on bounding-box accuracy. The figure compares predictions from LLaDA-V trained with default
linear masking (top) and with the proposed hybrid masking that combines linear and deterministic full masking (bottom). The linear-
masked model correctly predicts the action type but generates an inaccurate bounding box, missing the target region. In contrast, the
hybrid-masked model, guided by conditional refinement between anchor and extent coordinates, produces a precise bounding box that
accurately localizes the target element. The green bounding box is the ground truth and the red one is the prediction.
